question: What are the five Project Management Process Groups and their primary objectives?
expected: Initiating Process Group: define a new project or phase and obtain authorization.
Planning Process Group: establish project scope, refine objectives, and define the course of action.
Executing Process Group: complete the work defined in the project management plan to satisfy project requirements.
Monitoring and Controlling Process Group: track, review, and regulate project progress and performance; initiate changes if necessary.
Closing Process Group: formally complete or close the project, phase, or contract.
evidence: Project management processes are grouped into the following five Project Management Process Groups: Initiating Process Group. Those processes performed to define a new project or a new phase of an existing project by obtaining authorization to start the project or phase. Planning Process Group. Those processes required to establish the scope of the project, refine the objectives, and define the course of action required to attain the objectives that the project was undertaken to achieve. Executing Process Group. Those processes performed to complete the work defined in the project management plan to satisfy the project requirements. Monitoring and Controlling Process Group. Those processes required to track, review, and regulate the progress and performance of the project; identify any areas in which changes to the plan are required; and initiate the corresponding changes. Closing Process Group. Those processes performed to formally complete or close the project, phase, or contract.

evidence: The engagement level of stakeholders can be classified as follows: Unaware. Unaware of the project and potential impacts. Resistant. question: Hãy giải thích về Schedule Fast Tracking và Schedule Crashing trong quản lý dự án PMP.
expected: Schedule Fast Tracking là khi các hoạt động trên Critical Path được thực hiện song song (chồng lấn) để rút ngắn thời gian dự án.
Schedule Crashing là việc phê duyệt làm thêm giờ, thêm nguồn lực hoặc trả tiền để đẩy nhanh việc giao hàng của các hoạt động trên critical path.
Nhớ đến nguyên lý của lợi nhuận giảm dần, nơi thêm nhiều nguồn lực sẽ chỉ cải thiện lịch trình của bạn đến một mức độ nào đó - hiệu quả giảm khi bạn thêm nhiều hơn.
evidence: Schedule Fast Tracking is when activities on the Critical Path are done in parallel (overlapped) to shorten the project duration. Schedule crashing is approving overtime, adding resources, or paying to expedite delivery of activities on the critical path. Remember the law of diminishing returns, where adding more resources will only improve your schedule up to a point - the effect reduces the more you add.

question: How do the Critical Path Method and the Monitoring and Controlling Process Group contribute to effective project management?
expected: The Critical Path Method helps in identifying the sequence of activities that determine the project duration and allows for techniques like Schedule Fast Tracking and Schedule Crashing to optimize the schedule.
The law of diminishing returns applies to Schedule Crashing, indicating that adding more resources will only improve the schedule up to a certain point.
The Monitoring and Controlling Process Group ensures that project performance is regularly measured and analyzed to identify and correct variances from the project management plan.
This process group involves evaluating change requests, recommending corrective or preventive actions, and monitoring project activities against the project management plan and baselines.
Continuous monitoring within the Monitoring and Controlling Process Group provides stakeholders with insight into the project's status and helps in identifying areas requiring additional attention.
evidence: Schedule Fast Tracking is when activities on the Critical Path are done in parallel (overlapped) to shorten the project duration. Schedule crashing is approving overtime, adding resources, or paying to expedite delivery of activities on the critical path. Remember the law of diminishing returns, where adding more resources will only improve your schedule up to a point - the effect reduces the more you add.

The key benefit of this Process Group is that project performance is measured and analyzed at regular intervals, appropriate events, or when exception conditions occur in order to identify and correct variances from the project management plan.
